title: Understanding Bias-Variance Decomposition
text: The bias-variance decomposition is a way to express the error of a model in terms of bias, variance, and irreducible error (noise). It is typically used in regression problems. Consider how classification problems might differ.

title: Zero-One Loss in Classification
text: Zero-one loss is a metric used in classification tasks. It measures the accuracy of predictions by assigning a loss of $$1$$ for incorrect predictions and $$0$$ for correct ones. Think about how this might affect the applicability of bias-variance decomposition.

title: Consider the Nature of Decision Trees
text: Decision trees are often used for classification tasks. They split data into branches to make predictions. How might this structure impact the bias and variance in a classification context?
